interpretation: Instruction: 'grasp and insert the brown square nut onto the brown square block.' Robot: capx_robosuite_panda_nut, a 7-DOF Panda with a parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 8 cm, closing axis TCP x, approach TCP z, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95). Only one camera (birdview, straight down from (0.56, 0, 1.088); image right = +y, image down = +x). No wrist camera. Table at z = -0.0917. Brown square nut = obj1 at start: a square ring about 8.8 cm outer, 4.5 cm hole, 2 cm thick, ring center about (0.450, 0.186), with a 3.1 cm wide handle sticking out toward +y (y 0.227 to 0.269). Brown square block = the square peg at (0.789, 0.0985), 3.1-3.2 cm square, top at z = 0.038 (13 cm tall), dark sides and brown top; perception split it into obj3/obj4/obj5/obj6. The grey cylinder obj2 at (0.781, -0.098) is the other (round) peg, not the target. Goal: the nut threaded onto the square peg (peg through the hole) and resting at the bottom on the table. 'Insert onto' could arguably mean only partway on, but a careful reading is fully down, so that is what I aimed for.
plan: Initial plan: grasp the handle top-down with the fingers closing along world x (yaw 0), lift, carry the nut so the hole is over the peg, measure the alignment with the camera, lower onto the peg, release and retreat. Changes along the way: (1) The straight Cartesian path from the folded home pose crossed joint 2 = 0 and rotated at the same time, which made the IK flip q1/q3/q5 (2.09x the speed limit). I routed through a planar waypoint (0.40, 0, 0.12) with the orientation unchanged, then rotated and shifted to the pre-grasp. (2) Above the peg with the handle pointing +y, the arm was at its reach limit: exact top-down poses below z = 0.05 had 4-8 mm IK error, and the preview refused 'unreachable'. I rotated the gripper +90 deg about the vertical while holding the nut, so the handle pointed toward the robot. That moved the TCP 6.3 cm closer to the base while keeping the hole over the peg, and made deep poses easily reachable. (3) In that pose the wrist hid the hole from the only camera, so I aligned by geometry: precise RGB edge measurements of the visible ring edges unprojected at the known nut-top height, plus the nut dimensions measured from the start image. (4) Going all the way down while holding was not possible, because link 7 would reach the peg top below TCP z of about -0.015. So I pushed to TCP z = -0.002 (nut about 5.7 cm onto the peg) and released, letting the nut drop the remaining ~7 cm along the peg.

steps.what: Read the robot description, instruction and budget; listed objects and annotated the birdview image
steps.why: Identify the robot, camera, nut and peg
steps.result: 900 steps at 0.05 s (45 s of motion). obj1 = nut, obj3-6 = square peg (split), obj2 = round peg. Step 0.

steps.what: Measured the nut (heightmap of obj1 points), the table height, the peg top, and the finger and hand collision spheres
steps.why: Plan the grasp point and height, and the place target
steps.result: Handle center about (0.448, 0.249), 3.1-3.2 cm wide. Ring center about (0.450, 0.186). Peg top center about (0.788, 0.0985) at z 0.038. The TCP is at the finger-pad center (3.6 mm behind ee_pose); fingertips about 1.2 cm below the TCP. Grasp TCP z chosen as -0.075.
Yaw 180 gave a flipped arm near the q2 limit; chose yaw 0. A straight path was refused (2.09x too fast at a joint-2 = 0 crossing with q5 swinging 4 rad/s).

steps.why: Avoid the IK flip by crossing joint 2 = 0 in a planar motion
steps.result: Reached the grasp pose exactly, nut undisturbed (images/005). Step 142.
gripper_measured 0.615, gap 3.08 cm = handle width, so held. Step 162.

steps.what: Lifted to TCP z 0.12; measured the held nut from the point cloud
steps.why: Check grasp stability and the hole offset from the TCP
steps.result: Nut perfectly level, top 3 mm above the TCP (no slip). Hole center offset (0.000, -0.062) from the TCP. Perception showed a stale ghost obj1 on the table, then a 21 cm tall phantom obj7 for the held nut (hidden space filled in). I ignored it in collision checks. Step 194.

steps.what: Carried the nut to hover over the peg (TCP (0.7876, 0.1615, 0.075)) and measured alignment from a 3 mm heightmap
steps.why: Align the hole over the peg
steps.result: Hole center x 0.785 vs peg 0.7876 (-2.6 mm), y matched. Step 256.

steps.what: Tried to preview the descent to TCP z 0.020
steps.why: Engage the nut on the peg
steps.result: Refused: unreachable (8 mm IK error). The arm is at its reach limit at x = 0.79 with an exact top-down pose.

steps.what: Rotated the gripper +90 deg (yaw 90) while moving the TCP to (0.7246, 0.101), first at z 0.09, then a hover at 0.072 (3.0 s)
steps.why: Swing the handle toward the robot so the TCP is 6.3 cm closer to the base, keeping the hole over the peg
steps.result: Executed cleanly, grip unchanged (0.614). The wrist now hid the hole from the camera (images/011, 012). Step 322.

steps.what: Measured the visible outer ring edges at full RGB resolution (unprojected at nut-top z 0.0752), the nut dimensions from the start image, and the peg-top center from the start image (z 0.038). Defined an agent box obj11 for the full peg
steps.why: Align without seeing the hole; make collision checks cover the whole peg
steps.result: Hole center about (0.7855, 0.101) vs peg (0.7894, 0.0985); corrected the TCP by (+3.9, -2.6) mm to (0.7285, 0.0984).

steps.why: Engage the nut about 2.5 cm onto the peg
steps.result: TCP reached the target exactly, status done, grip unchanged. The cloud showed the nut top at z 0.033, below the 0.038 peg top, so the peg was through the hole. Step 354.

steps.what: Checked how deep the hand could go while holding
steps.why: Push the nut down as far as safely possible
steps.result: Link 7 would reach the peg top below TCP z of about -0.015. Chose -0.002.

steps.what: Pushed down to TCP z -0.002 (1.0 s), then opened the gripper (1 s)
steps.why: Put the nut ~5.7 cm onto the peg, then release it to drop the rest of the way
steps.result: Reached the target, gripper opened (gap 7.8 cm), held None. Step 400.

steps.what: Retreated straight up to z 0.12, then to (0.45, 0.30, 0.22) (2.6 s)
steps.why: Clear the fingers and stop the arm hiding the peg from the camera
steps.result: Clean, no contacts. The birdview showed the nut flat around the peg (images/015, 016). Step 458.

steps.what: Verified with reperceive, the point cloud and a closeup render; called finish_episode
steps.why: Check the final state before finishing
steps.result: Nut obj13 top at z -0.0722 (same as when it lay on the table at the start, std 0.1 mm, no tilt). Ring centered about (0.788, 0.098) on the peg (0.789, 0.0985), peg points inside the hole. Round peg obj2 untouched. Finished at step 458 of 900.

key_images.caption: Start: nut with handle toward +y at upper right; square peg (brown top) and round grey peg at the bottom
Start object ids: obj1 nut, obj3-6 square peg (split), obj2 round peg
Open gripper lowered around the handle
Nut lifted level in the grip
Hovering at yaw 0: peg top visible through the hole (parallax shifts it up-left)

Final 3D closeups from four azimuths: nut obj13 at the base of peg obj11

lessons: 1) On this Panda the folded home pose (q2 = -1.585) makes straight Cartesian moves to low targets cross joint 2 = 0 while rotating, and the IK flips. A planar first waypoint (same orientation, y = 0) gives a smooth path. 2) The square peg at x of about 0.79 is at the edge of reach for an exact top-down pose below z of about 0.05 when the TCP is on the far side (+y). Holding the nut so the handle points toward the robot keeps the TCP 6 cm closer and makes the insertion easy to reach; decide this before the transport (rotate during the carry) to save a step. 3) With the birdview as the only camera, the wrist hides the hole once the handle points toward the robot. Measure the hole-to-TCP offset while it is visible (after the lift), and align by geometry. Full-resolution RGB edges unprojected at a known height were more precise than the 3-4 mm depth grid. 4) Perception fills hidden space under a held object (a 21 cm phantom) and keeps stale ghosts; ignore or replace those ids in check_batch, and add an agent box for a partly occluded fixture like the peg. 5) Link 7 limits how deep the hand can push a handle-held nut down a 13 cm peg; releasing once the nut is ~5 cm onto the peg worked, and the nut slid to the table. 6) A TCP that reaches its commanded depth with an unchanged grip reading is a good proprioceptive sign that the nut went onto the peg rather than landing on its top.
